Subject: Request: EU pilot evidence (VPC controls + retention)

Hi Connor,

We're getting the final approval threads moving for the MedicoHealth pilot (EU region). Security has asked for a short evidence pack so we can close the internal SIG/CAIQ review. Specifically they asked for:

- A VPC/private deployment diagram showing logical boundaries and peering (certified endpoints).
- Confirmation of key management boundaries (where KMS/HSM lives for EU tenants).
- Data retention defaults and options for token/log retention (we need both minimum and maximum retention windows).
- A filled SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet (or pointer to answers) and any SOC 2 excerpts relevant to access controls.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a top-level diagram + a short summary (1 page) for each of the bullets above by Dec 10? Also let me know if there are any customer-specific exceptions we should track for procurement.

Thanks,

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the clear list. We're on it. High level notes up front:

- We can provide a VPC topology (logical) and an operator-runbook snippet for private peering and fallback routes.
- EU tenant keystores can be integrated with customer-managed KMS in most cases; our default is Redwood-managed keys with region partitioning. We'll include both options in the summary.
- Retention: default runtime telemetry is 30 days; customer-configurable logs/token retention can be reduced to 0 (ephemeral) or extended to 365 days depending on contract and storage options. We'll provide exact knobs and where they're enforced.
- We'll attach a SOC 2 controls extract focused on access control / encryption in transit & at rest, and a preliminary SIG/CAIQ draft.

Targeting Dec 9 for a full pack so you have a day for internal review. If you need it sooner, please flag which items are must-have.

Action: Marissa, Sean — can you assemble the diagram + SOC2 extract and SIG draft? I'll coordinate final review and package.

Connor

Connor / Sean —

Attaching the first-pass artifacts for internal review. Highlights and careful callouts below.

1) redwood_vpc_network_diagram_v1.pdf (attached) — logical diagram showing:
   - Customer VPC peering via PrivateLink to Redwood ingress endpoints in eu-west-1.
   - Tenant isolation: per-tenant subnet pools and per-instance security groups.
   - Control plane remains in Redwood-managed control plane (customer data path is segregated).

2) SOC2-snapshot-2026Q3.pdf (attached) — excerpted pages for CC6/CC7 where relevant to key management and access logging. Note: full SOC 2 report is shared under NDA; this excerpt is intended for procurement/security review.

3) SIG-answers-medicopilot.xlsx (attached) — completed for the VPC / crypto / data retention sections. Items still marked "TBD" are operational playbook items we need to confirm with infra (low risk).

4) retention-policy-extract.txt (attached) — explicit configurable keys: token_retention_days, log_retention_days, audit_log_retention_days. Defaults called out and policy for emergency retention extension.

Risk items to surface to MedicoHealth:
- If customer requests customer-managed KMS in their own project, we need vaulting details; that takes ~5 business days to validate once keys are provisioned.
- If the pilot requires absolute zero-data-retention at all layers (including telemetry used for inference routing), we need to assess fallbacks; some observability breadcrumbs remain for operational SLOs.

I'll let Sean add the operational confirmation notes. Once reviewed we'll package into a single shareable folder for Claire.

Marissa

From: sean.gallagher@redwoodinc.com
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinc.com, connor.obrien@redwoodinc.com
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 08:50:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: EU pilot evidence (VPC controls + retention)

Quick operational clarifications to include in the pack (we should add as a single page):

- KMS: Redwood-managed KMS keys are region-specific and do not leave eu-west-1. Customer-managed KMS access is supported via cross-account grants; we will include the grant template and required IAM principals.
- Network egress: PrivateLink endpoints terminate inside the customer's VPC; egress to third parties follows the customer's routing table unless explicit Redwood egress is requested (we'll document options).
- Audit trails: Access logs (admin console/API) are retained for 90 days by default; audit_log_retention_days can be extended per contract. All access logs are hashed and stored in encrypted S3 buckets scoped to the deployment.
- Token handling: Inference token payloads are not stored persistently unless caching is enabled; caching TTL is configurable and off by default for pilots that require minimal retention.

Marissa — please fold these lines into the final one-pager. Connor — I'll be available for the call if MedicoHealth wants to walk through the diagrams.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Field Engineering — Redwood Inference
